newsitem.title: USA: Brazil's CSN official defends investments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CSN official defends investments.

text.p: A senior executive for Brazilian steel-maker Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) on Wednesday defended the company's investment of hundreds of millions of dollars in rail and steel companies as a protection for the core business.

Jose Marcos Treiger, head of investor relations for CSN, said CSN, Latin America's biggest steel company, made the investments this year to guarantee the future of its integrated steel plant at Volta Redonda in Rio de Janeiro state.

"CSN is absolutely not becoming an out of focus company, is not becoming a holding company, is not becoming an conglomerate," Treiger told a conference on Latin American steel companies sponsored by Salomon Brothers.

He said the investments including 240 million reais (about $240 million dollars) in recently privatized power company Light Servicos de Eletricidade SA, were necessary to help safeguard CSN's 1.2 billion reais ($1.2 billion dollars) investment planned through the year 2000 for its plant.
"We are reducing risks that might -- might-- pop up in the future in my country," he said.
If CSN had not invested in light, for example, "we could be standing in a room like this and explaining why we did not guarantee a supply of energy to an enormous plant."
The investments also include $65 million in two power plants and $58 million in newly privatized rail companies that carry much of CSN's 10 million tonnes of ore and coal each year.
Treiger said CSN would produce from 4.5 million to 4.6 million tonnes of steel this year, the limit of the company's capacity.

That production could rise to 5.1 million tonnes in 1998 with the expansion at Volta Redonda. He added that CSN should see strong growth in its galvanized steel business as the Brazilian automobile industry expanded .
